criticise: Can you criticise my poster and tell me what to change?
Please criticise my drawing gently, because I want to make it better.
The judges will criticise each model, then suggest ways to make it stronger.
recognise: Would you recognise your old teacher if you saw her at the shops?
I can always recognise my cat by her white paws.
Birdwatchers learn to recognise each bird by its song.
sacrifice: Mum made a sacrifice and gave up her free Saturday for my party.
Is it a sacrifice to miss football so you can help a friend?
Giving up her seat on the bus was a small sacrifice.
definite: We need a definite time for the picnic, not just maybe.
Is it definite that we are going to the seaside on Sunday?
There is a definite smell of toast coming from the kitchen!
desperate: The little puppy was desperate for a drink after the long walk.
In a desperate hunt for the last jigsaw piece, we searched under the sofa.
Why are you so desperate to open your birthday presents?
immediate: My immediate reaction was to laugh, with no time to think.
The immediate task was to put the wet washing inside before the rain.
Her immediate thought on seeing the cake was to taste it right away.
immediately: When the bell rang, we lined up immediately.
The ice cream melted almost immediately in the hot sun!
Did the puppy come immediately when you called its name?
competition: Who will win the sandcastle competition on the beach today?
The egg and spoon race is my favourite competition on sports day.
Our class entered the cake baking competition at the school fair.
explanation: Can you give me an explanation for why the cake sank?
The teacher gave a clear explanation of how rainbows form.
His explanation of the game rules was so clear that we all understood.
pronunciation: Reading aloud helps me with my pronunciation of long words!
The word is hard to spell, but its pronunciation is easy.
Is the pronunciation of this word the same as the one in the song?
